mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is persistent and not dependent on specific rate levels.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5% annualized, the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain or increase interest rates, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP and housing starts signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which drives positive equity returns as corporate earnings rise. The effect is multiplicative and only occurs when both indicators are positive.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST show positive growth (t-test p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%), labor market tightness drives wage growth and corporate profit margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days. This effect is absent during high unemployment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across business cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising (t-test p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly job gains exceed 200,000 (PAYEMS > 200000), it signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 200000 (t-test p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) is high and the Fed is raising rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the market anticipates prolonged monetary tightening, causing negative equity returns. The effect is multiplicative and only occurs when both conditions are met.
regime_hint: high inflation and rate hike cycle
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high consumer spending (RSAFS > 700,000), retail sales growth fuels corporate revenue expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days. This effect is strongest during economic expansions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 700000 (t-test p-value > 0.05).
